text:
Elaine: Quick heads-up — docs PR #4382 has tenant quota examples that still show `max_replicas` instead of the new `min_capacity`/`burst_capacity` flags.
Pranav: Ah thanks, I missed that when I copied the old snippets. Should we keep both forms and add a migration note?
Elaine: Prefer to show the new schema as primary and add a short migration section. We don't need both snippets inline, just a small table mapping old->new.
Sam: I'll volunteer to update the SDK example for JS/py. Which repo is the canonical snippet in? link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/blob/main/dedicated/capacity.md
Pranav: It's in that file + the code-samples repo. For the SDK snippet, replace `client.reserve({ max_replicas: 8 })` with:
```js
// JS SDK (example)
await client.reserve({
  min_capacity: 4,
  burst_capacity: 8,
  labels: { team: 'search' }
})
```
Maria: Also call out the isolation behavior: reserved pools with `tenancy: dedicated` will force node isolation; add a one-line sentence in the table.
Elaine: Good call. Also we should clarify SLA phrasing — change "best-effort" to "SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated" in the handbook intro.
Sam: I'll PR the SDK change and push a tiny migration section. Can someone review the wording for the migration mapping? I'll tag you @Pranav for a quick pass.
Pranav: Reviewing now. Small nit: the YAML sample should use `reserved_pools:` top-level not `pools:` — the old docs had the wrong key.
Elaine: Example YAML to include in the migration section:
```yaml
reserved_pools:
  - name: enterprise
    tenancy: dedicated
    min_capacity: 4
    burst_capacity: 8
    labels:
      team: search
```
Maria: Adding a short note: customers using `max_replicas` with autoscale policies should map to `burst_capacity` for short bursts and `min_capacity` for baseline.
DocsBot: build-docs-staging succeeded for PR 4384 :white_check_mark:
Sam: Thanks — I'll open PR 4384 now with the changes, will mark as `docs/needs-review`.
Elaine: Quick checklist before merging: update JS/py SDK snippets, add YAML migration snippet, fix handbook SLA sentence, and add a link to the SDK reference. If all green, merge and deploy.
Maria: I can review in ~30m :eyes:
Sam: sweet, thanks everyone :rocket:
